title: Prove it or lose it
summary: Three questions to connect the whole marketing investment to the next business decision.
text: Every CMO knows this meeting. The CFO slides the budget across the table and asks one question. Prove it or lose it. My own budget was cut twice in 10 years. Once for COVID, once for a measurement battle we frankly got wrong. What's helped me since is checking whether the measurement covers the same ground as the budget. Creator spend, influencer packages, retail media, the deals that never touch a dashboard. If those are missing from the picture, it's harder to explain what the whole investment is doing. So, I come back to three questions. Can you see every spend line? Can you compare what each one contributed? And does the answer arrive in time to help with the next decision? The thing I wish I'd had then back when I had legacy MMM is what we have today. Full Commerce MMM. The real full picture of go-to-market investments. all 10 spend lines in one picture. And the third question is where most enterprises fall down. The insight arrives, but the action doesn't. Not in time to change the next decision. This is a whole new world, though. Um, an AI interface that's learned on 10 years of MMM expert context, not just Claude or ChatGPT. Ask the question in plain language, run a live simulation in the meeting, and act on it while the market is still there. That's what keeps me engaged. what's possible. Now, I've sat in that chair for 20 plus years as a CMO. These days, I'm focused on paying it forward, sharing what I learned with the next generation of leaders. The shift that helped me most is being able to sit down with finance and say, "Here's what we're seeing. Here's what we've learned, and here's where the next dollar could help us grow. Faster, smarter, better decisions." If that's you, let's chat or start with my AI twin on aicatalyst.biz. It knows how I think about this.

title: Where does the next dollar go?
summary: Randy explores brand agents, individual shopping conversations and scheduled live selling shows.
text: You proved it. The budget's yours. Now comes the harder question. Where does the next dollar go? Search, the front door of the internet for 20 years, is shifting. Your customer doesn't search anymore. Their agent does. 10 million people set up Meta's Muse in 6 weeks in the US and Canada alone. Amazon blocked it. Walmart and Shopify opened the door. And look at Google. Half a trillion dollars gone in a single day. Its worst day ever. Its own AI answers are eating its search ads. That's the market pricing in the end of the search box. So when your customer's agent comes knocking, who meets them? The way I look at it, the next dollar doesn't go to the search box. It goes to a brand agent on your own storefront, a digital human, your best salesperson, one-to-one around the clock, connected to your real inventory, your bundles, your margin. The experience hasn't changed in 25 years. Search box, scroll, click, the death scroll. The agent ends that. Just a conversation. And a conversation qualifies, guides, and converts. So the traffic you get is better traffic. More of what we buy happens online every year. If no one's there to meet that agent, the opportunity is gone. There's a second way in, one to many. a live show at a set time for a special launch, your brand agent hosting it, or even an influencer’s twin as your brand agent. Real people joining in. Folks love being part of an exclusive event. When the conversation happens, one-to-one or one to many, it's built around the customer. That's what drives higher consideration. The brands that build this now are the ones the agents recommend first. That's Agentic Commerce. I've spent 20 plus years as a CMO. These days, I'm focused on paying it forward, sharing what I learned with the next generation of leaders. Faster, smarter, better decisions. If that's you, let's chat or start with my AI twin on aicatalyst.biz. It knows how I think about this.
